Where it began

Amir Jangoo was born on 14 July 1997. He is a left-handed batsman and wicketkeeper from Trinidad, and his first taste of senior cricket came in January 2015, when the West Indies Under-19s played in the Regional Super50.

Two years later, in April 2017, he first played first-class cricket, for Trinidad and Tobago in the Regional Four Day Competition. In 2020 he joined the Trinbago Knight Riders and made his Twenty20 debut for them in the Caribbean Premier League on 2 September. He went on to play in the league for the Antigua and Barbuda Falcons.

The player

His international call came in December 2024, for a one-day series against Bangladesh. He made his debut in the third match, on 12 December, and scored an unbeaten 104. He was only the second West Indian to make a hundred on his ODI debut. His Test career began in 2025.

June 2026 brought his finest days. In the first Test against Sri Lanka he reached his maiden Test hundred from 226 balls, then kept going to 233. With his captain, Roston Chase, he put on 401 for the sixth wicket, the biggest sixth-wicket stand in Test history at the time.

By November 2026 he had played seven Tests and made 508 runs at 50.80, with two hundreds and a best of 233. With the gloves on he had taken three catches and a stumping.

What made him special

Jangoo has a happy knack of turning a start into something large. By November 2026 he had passed fifty twice in Test cricket, and both times he had gone on to a hundred. Fifties, it seemed, were for other people.

He can score fast as well as long. In a one-day international against India on 30 September 2026 he reached three figures in 70 balls and finished with 114 from 77, his best in ODIs, as the West Indies made 405, a team record. India chased down 406 to win anyway. Some days the game simply belongs to the other side, however well you bat.

And finally

For a long time Jangoo waited patiently in domestic cricket, almost ten years from his Under-19 debut to his first match for the West Indies. He then made up for lost time with a hundred on his ODI debut and a double hundred in Tests. Good things, as the saying goes, come to those who wait. In his case they came in big helpings.
